{"decision":"NOT SETTLED. Today the backend is chosen by which constructor runs, and RocksDB is a Cargo feature — so evaluating in-memory against the persistent store means building a second binary. The question is whether a running server should be told which backend to use (a flag, an environment variable, a per-design setting), or whether compile-time selection is the right answer and the consumer's real need is met some other way.

WHO NEEDS IT AND WHY: raised by @ajs from flo2's 2026-09-13 session. flo2 has an open question of its own that it cannot evaluate without either a second binary or a runtime selector.

WHAT IS ALREADY RULED, and it bears on this without answering it: dec:idea-a-byte-backend-that-compiles-in-seconds was REJECTED 2026-09-11 — RocksDB stays, because an engine swap forces a migration on every consumer to save build time on the builder's machine. That rejection was about REPLACING the engine. This asks whether both may be reachable from one binary, which is a different question and is not foreclosed by it.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO RECORD: a runtime selector makes "which backend is this design in" a property of how the server was launched rather than of the design directory, and a design opened under the wrong backend would present as empty — the same silent failure mode dec:one-process-many-stores already names for identity.
